newsitem.title: GERMANY: Special charges hit Lufthansa 96 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Special charges hit Lufthansa 96 earnings.

text.p: German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG said on Thursday that its 1996 operating profit was just below its pre-tax profit figure of almost 700 marks.

In a statement issued in response to an article in the German business magazine Capital, Lufthansa said that its 1996 figures would not match those seen in 1995. It is due to report its 1996 results on May 7.
The group said that it had 320 million marks in extra charges relating to higher fuel prices in the second half of 1996.
This combined with 110 million marks in additional pension provisions, resulting in extraordinary charges of 430 million marks over the year.
"Without these extraordinary items Lufthansa would have reported clearly higher earnings on an operational and consolidated basis," Lufthansa said in the statement.

"The figures cited by Capital are wrong," Lufthansa said, referring to the report, to be published on Friday, which claimed that the financial situation at the airline was worse than Lufthansa itself had claimed.
"Lufthansa is totally against the use of cosmetic accounting. The annual results will be examined by auditors as in any other public company," Lufthansa said.
